extracted.intended_audience: academics and practitioners serving as peer reviewers for the Journal of Open Initiatives in Academic Libraries (JOI)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for performing open peer review of manuscripts submitted to JOI (library & information science focus), including reviewer responsibilities, ethical rules, confidentiality, timelines, recommended feedback practices, and recommendation categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open Review Process
rubrics_metrics.description: An open review process is an element of the open research ecosystem and supports transparency. For JOI, both the author(s) and reviewers' names are shared throughout the entire process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Open review is as rigorous as other review models and requires reviewers to act ethically and transparently. The review (including reviewer name and institutional affiliation) will be published alongside the manuscript at the time of publication. Reviewers are encouraged to include the publication on their researcher profiles. The editorial board will ensure no violations of ethical conduct during the open peer review process; conflicts arising will be handled by the Editors-in-Chief. Any reviewers or authors conducting themselves outside of these expectations will forfeit their right to inclusion in the publication and their acceptance will be terminated immediately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer reviewer responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer reviewers should see their role as fundamental to the development and protection of the journal’s quality: ensure every paper recommended for publication is well-written, well-researched, and makes a significant contribution to the existing knowledge base.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers must read papers thoroughly to identify flaws and also make recommendations to the author(s) on how the paper might be improved. Spend appropriate and necessary time to provide a thorough and unbiased review. If you do not have sufficient time or the paper is outside your expertise or presents a conflict of interest, inform the editors so an alternative reviewer can be assigned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain a constructive and impartial tone
rubrics_metrics.description: Please strive to maintain a positive, impartial attitude toward the manuscript; the position of the peer reviewer should be that of the author’s ally, with the aim of promoting effective and accurate communication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When preparing comments for authors, present criticism dispassionately and avoid abrasive comments. Constructive and positive comments help authors develop their work; unconsidered, thoughtless comments will discourage authors' future involvement in writing for publication. Find positive, encouraging things to say; even small compliments are appreciated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider international context and non-native English authors
rubrics_metrics.description: JOI is an international journal; reviewers should consider this when commenting on both content and style of the article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Topics of interest and terminology may vary among countries; readers may not be familiar with colloquialisms or region-specific expressions. Suggest clarification of terms that may be ambiguous to international readers (e.g., academic ranks, bureaucratic structures) and be mindful that authors whose first language is not English may require additional work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality
rubrics_metrics.description: An unpublished manuscript is a privileged document and must be handled in the strictest confidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protect the manuscript from any and all forms of exploitation or misuse. The manuscript or any portion of it must not be reproduced, circulated, cited, or referred to prior to its publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict of interest (COI)
rubrics_metrics.description: Before reviewing, the reviewer should ensure there is no conflict of interest in reviewing the paper and must declare any conflicts prior to accepting the appointment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a conflict exists, contact the section editor immediately so an alternative reviewer can be assigned. COI must be declared promptly and honestly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical violations in a paper under review (disqualifying features)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the manuscript contains serious ethical violations the reviewer should discontinue the review and notify the editorial board.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disqualifying features listed include plagiarism, fabricated results, and absence of IRB approval or unethical procedures for human research. Notify the editorial board immediately if any of these are detected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accepting or rejecting a review request (timeliness & suitability)
rubrics_metrics.description: Only accept manuscripts for which you are confident you can provide a timely and high-quality review; do not accept to gain access to the full paper if you cannot review it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accept or decline a review promptly; the deadline to accept or decline is seven days from the date of the request. If you decline, provide a reason to help editors assign manuscripts better in the future. If you are no longer interested in reviewing for the journal, inform the editors so your name can be removed from the list.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide comprehensive, evidence-based feedback
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer reviewers are required to evaluate the manuscript critically and constructively and to provide valid and informative comments to authors and editors which will facilitate improvement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider all aspects of the draft. Fully explain problems rather than making unsupported statements (e.g., instead of saying a paper 'seems disorganized,' explain what is disorganized using specific details). Suggest ways to correct problems, identify unclear or ambiguous passages, possible reorganization, or the need for condensing. If the manuscript includes repeated instances needing correction, provide one or two examples. Base comments on accepted guidelines, concepts, and rules rather than personal style. Read the draft several times, using the first reading to look for high-level matters such as interest level, general organization, and clarity of discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declare limits of your expertise
rubrics_metrics.description: If there is an aspect of the research methodology or subject area in which you lack expertise, inform the editor that you did not provide comments in that area.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors assign manuscripts to peer reviewers based on areas of expertise; they may have chosen other reviewers to complement your expertise. If you think you do not have the expertise or skills required to properly review the manuscript, inform the editor and decline the review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feedback etiquette regarding acceptability
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not make specific comments about the acceptability of an article in your comments for transmission to the author; suggested revisions should not be expressed as conditions of acceptance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may give the editors your opinion regarding overall acceptability in the editor-only space, but avoid telling authors that making certain changes will guarantee acceptance. Editors base decisions on evaluations from multiple reviewers and are not obligated to honor every recommendation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation options and their meanings
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers must indicate a recommendation to the editor using the provided options.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The options for JOI are: 'Accept submission' (in scope, meets requirements, no changes other than copyediting), 'Revisions required' (in scope, meets most requirements, revisions recommended), 'Resubmit for review' (in scope but does not meet requirements; significant revisions requiring another round of peer review), 'Resubmit elsewhere' (not applicable to JOI), 'Decline submission' (out of scope or does not meet requirements even with major revisions), and 'See comments' (use only in exceptional circumstances; elaborate in editor-only comments). Note that editors may request additional reviewers and are not bound to reviewer recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Peer Review Template
rubrics_metrics.description: A peer review template will be available to guide reviewers on the questions they will be asked to answer when reviewing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep in mind that not all questions will apply to every paper and some papers may present other questions not included in the template; use it as a guide for thorough, consistent evaluations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognition of reviewer contribution
rubrics_metrics.description: The journal acknowledges and credits the work that goes into conducting a peer review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publishing the review (including reviewer name and institutional affiliation) alongside the manuscript is intended to acknowledge reviewers' labor and encourage inclusion on researcher profiles. This transparency aims to mitigate overlooked peer review work and create a constructive publishing space.
